_why: Six markets read this site and the price table states three KRW amounts,
because those are the only prices that exist: Korea is the launch store and
App Store Connect has no price points for the others yet. For three rounds
the page answered that by printing nothing — 'we are not printing a
converted figure' — which is honest about the exchange rate and useless to
a reader in Berlin trying to decide whether ₩1,900 is one coffee or one
So each market gets a SIZE, never a price. The numbers below are coarse
on purpose — 1.40, 11, 28, not 1.43, 11.07, 28.79 — so that they read as an
order of magnitude rather than a quote, and every sentence that carries
them says Apple charges by price point, not by exchange rate. The app never
needed this: PaywallView prints StoreKit's own displayPrice for whatever
storefront the reader is in.
This file is the single place they are written. check-content [22] holds
every dictionary's pr.approxref and n.hero.b5 to these exact tokens and to
that market's own currency, so no one language can drift to a different
figure, and replacing the estimates with the real store prices is an edit
here plus six sentences — not a hunt through six dictionaries.
asOf is the month the estimates were struck. When it is more than a year
old, restrike them or delete the line from the copy.
